buyer_question: A hackathon judge asks: does the finished repository do what its README claims, from a clean clone, with no credentials?

claims.text: From a clean clone, `./repro.sh` runs to completion with exit code 0 using only Python 3.10+ (no make, no docker, no credentials).
claims.source_quote: Level 1 needs only Python 3.10+ and reproduces every number in this README from the shipped proof.

claims.text: `python3 tests/test_scorer.py` passes all seven scorer contract tests.
`python3 eval/validate_cases.py` reports 20 case files checked and all valid.
`python3 -m eval.replay --run <advanced-v2-rescored run id>` reproduces the stored raw score 0.836 exactly.
Regenerating RESULTS.md and the README tables from proof/ yields files byte-identical to the committed ones.
claims.source_quote: REPRO OK: README/RESULTS regenerate byte-identically from proof
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m eval.report > RESULTS.md; python3 eval/render_readme.py; git diff --quiet -- README.md RESULTS.md

claims.text: Every git hash cited in RESULTS.md rows exists in the repository history (rows marked 'rewritten' carry a note instead of a hash).
claims.source_quote: Every table row carries its proof id, git hash and UTC timestamp
claims.probe_hint: for h in $(grep -oE '\| [0-9a-f]{7} \|' RESULTS.md | tr -d '| ' | sort -u); do git cat-file -e $h^{commit}; done

claims.text: The README's `repro` workflow badge asserts the latest run of that workflow on master succeeded.
`arms/PROMPTS.md` is generated from the arm sources: running `python3 tools/render_prompts.py` leaves it unchanged.
claims.source_quote: rendered from source by tools/render_prompts.py, do not edit by hand

claims.text: The repository's Releases contain a tag named submission-<sha> with a zip archive attached whose name contains the same sha.
claims.source_quote: The submitted commit is tagged `submission-<sha>` under Releases, with a `git archive` zip of exactly that commit attached
claims.probe_hint: GitHub API: releases -> tag_name starts with submission-, assets[0].name contains the sha (network on)

claims.text: The README results table contains held-out rows scored on both the untouched draft truth and the evidence-corrected truth, and `TRUTH_DIR=truth-draft python3 -m eval.replay --run <baseline-heldout run id>` runs successfully against `eval/truth-draft/`.
claims.source_quote: `TRUTH_DIR=truth-draft python3 -m eval.replay --run <id>` scores a run against the drafts
claims.probe_hint: grep 'scored on the untouched draft truth' README.md; TRUTH_DIR=truth-draft python3 -m eval.replay --run <baseline-heldout id>
